hero-description: "The glow up: self-reinvention and the need for validation through appearance"
s1-sub: The term "glow up" refers to a positive transformation — often of one's appearance — staged on social media and perceived as an indicator of success or social recognition.
s1-p1: This phenomenon intrigued me. Why such enthusiasm? More broadly, what does it reveal about our relationship to beauty, identity, and social dynamics?
s1-p2: So I chose to make it the subject of my thesis ✏️
s1-p3: → One thing led to another, and I arrived at this research question:
s1-p4: How does the glow up phenomenon, through the social dynamics of social media, become a tool of validation — both personal and social — shaping identity through appearance?
img1-caption: YouTube video thumbnails on the glow up
s2-p1: I began with a bibliographic review to understand the history of the phenomenon and explore its sociological, cultural and media angles. This gave me a historical depth on the origins of the glow up, and interpretive frameworks for my field observations.
s2-p2: I then studied the glow up in practice on YouTube and TikTok: analyzing videos, discourses and stagings, and observing comments to understand audience interactions and reactions.
s3-p1: From my observations, I structured my data using screenshots (thumbnails, frames, posts) and an analysis table on Google Sheets and Figma, grouping titles, metadata and observations for each studied piece of content.
s3-p2: I then defined a typology of the glow up, to categorize the different forms the phenomenon takes in practice. This step allowed me to structure my argument, substantiate my conclusions, put my field observations in perspective, and create a dialogue between field and bibliography.
s3-p3: This typology was represented as a map on Miro, to visualize the dynamics between each type and reveal the links between the different forms of the glow up.
s3-p4: Once all the argumentative elements were in place in my thesis outline, I moved on to writing.
s4-p1: The thesis was a major challenge. It was the first time I researched a little-studied subject like the glow up. It allowed me to discover a genuine enthusiasm for discovery, research and analysis. I gained academic understanding and analytical skills I didn't have before, coming from a more technical background.
s4-p2: → Writing this thesis is one of the factors that guided me toward UX, and more specifically toward UX research.
